courses.title: Build Your First Cash Flow Forecast
courses.summary: See next month’s cash before it arrives. Build a simple one-month forecast you can update in 10 minutes a week.
description: Most small businesses that run short of cash are profitable on paper. The problem is timing: customers pay late while rent, payroll and HST are due on fixed dates.

In this course, Ottawa bookkeeper Sara Haddad walks you through cash coming in and cash going out, then you build a real one-month forecast for your own business using our worksheet. Sara reviews your forecast and sends feedback.
suits: Anyone who has been surprised by a low bank balance
First-year owners preparing to talk to a bank
outcomes: Sort every payment into cash coming in and cash going out
Build a one-month, week-by-week cash flow forecast
Spot a short week early and pick one action to fix it
materials: A list of unpaid customer invoices

lessons.title: Cash coming in and going out
Pick one task to hand to AI

body: Profit and cash are not the same thing. This short welcome explains why a forecast gives you time to act.
Sort every dollar into two lists. Record customer payments on the day you expect the money, not the day you send the invoice.
Download the worksheet below. It has one column for each week of the month and fills in totals for you.
1. Enter your opening cash: the balance in your business bank account on the first day of the month.
2. Under Cash coming in, enter the customer payments you expect each week. Use the date the money will arrive, not the invoice date.
3. Under Cash going out, enter rent, payroll, supplier bills, HST remittances, loan payments and what you pay yourself.
4. Check the Closing cash row. If any week ends below zero, write one action you will take, such as calling a customer about a late invoice or moving a supplier payment.
A simple split for a $200 budget, and why the free channels come first.

assignments.brief: Use the worksheet to build a forecast for next month for your own business. Fill in opening cash, cash coming in and cash going out for each week. If any week ends below zero, add one action you will take. You can use rounded numbers. Sara only sees your submission, not your bank account.
rubric: Opening cash and four weeks filled in (4 marks)
Cash in recorded on expected payment dates (3 marks)
A clear action for any short week (3 marks)

assignments.brief: Write a one-page plan for spending $200 on local marketing over the next 30 days. List each channel, how much you will spend on it, and how you will know which customers it brought in.
rubric: Every dollar of the $200 is assigned to a channel (4 marks)
Free channels set up first (3 marks)
A way to track where each customer came from (3 marks)
